options.content:
## Decision

Volume-banded gating on the experience APIs in the selected **source** `$region`: **p99** when requests/5min >= `$p99_min_requests`, **p95** when >= `$min_requests`, otherwise **not judged**.

The sustained path is a **duty-cycle** test (`$sustain_min / $sustain_window_min`) with an honest-sample guard - not a raw breach-minute count.

Three distinct absent/neutral states on the gate: **CLEAR** (dark) means judged healthy; **TOO FEW REQUESTS** (grey) means data is arriving but not enough to judge; **NO DATA - FEED SILENT** (purple) means nothing arrived in `$stale_grace_min` minutes - after a failover that is itself a signal. Grey and purple are never merged.

panels.title: Failover gate (liveness ${stale_grace_min} min; duty ${sustain_min}/${sustain_window_min})
panels.description: Verdict for latency on the experience APIs in the selected source region. Scores: 0 CLEAR (dark), 1 WATCH (orange), 2 FAILOVER? (red), 3 TOO FEW REQUESTS (neutral grey), empty/noValue = NO DATA - FEED SILENT (purple). TOO FEW REQUESTS means data is arriving but there is not enough of it to judge. NO DATA - FEED SILENT means nothing has arrived in the last ${stale_grace_min} minutes. PRESENCE = (count(GATING_LAG) >= 1) * (sum(count_over_time(raw p99[stale_grace])) >= 1): volume band satisfied AND a genuinely fresh latency sample inside the grace window (raw range, not offset/lookback). SCORE_FINAL = SCORE * liveness so feed-silent shares the same $stale_grace_min horizon. Volume-banded gating wrapped in sum without(__name__). or (liveness*3) is TOO FEW when SCORE_FINAL is empty but the feed is alive.

options.content:
## Method / known limits

This board is a **customer-shaped** reference implementation of an internal failover-readiness design on Temporal Cloud OpenMetrics (`prometheus-kind`). The SQL does not port. Only the decision design does. Build it as if the namespace carries sustained traffic.

### Inherited thresholds (unvalidated on this surface)

These numbers come from an internal scan of **1,190 accounts** and are **inherited, not re-derived** here. Treat them as starting points, not as validated for this account:

- `$lat_ceiling_s` (default 0.2s)
- `$sustain_min` / `$sustain_window_min` (default 5 / 10 → 50% duty)
- `$sev_multiple` (default 25× ceiling)
- `$breadth_min` (default 2 namespaces)
- `$p99_min_requests` / `$min_requests` (default 1000 / 100 requests per 5 min)

The sustained path's **false-alarm rate has never been measured**.

### Volume-band union must collapse `__name__`

Wrap the p99-or-p95 gating union in `sum without(__name__) (...)`. Inside a range subquery both arms can appear for the same series when volume crosses `$p99_min_requests` mid-window; `count_over_time` / `max_over_time` drop `__name__` and the two collapse into one labelset, aborting the query with `vector cannot contain metrics with the same labelset`. Ordinary diurnal traffic variation is enough. A broken query must not render as NO DATA - FEED SILENT.

### Calibration that *was* measured here

- `$stale_grace_min` defaults to **7** (not the reference board's 3) because this endpoint publishes ~**209s (~3.5 min)** behind wall clock. A 3-minute liveness window is permanently empty on this surface.
- `$publication_lag_min` defaults to **4** to clear that lag on windowed subquery counts and on the lagged instant terms (WATCH / severity / gating-presence). Offset alone does **not** fix mid-window carry-forward on gapped series (see duty-cycle section).

### Duty-cycle and subquery carry-forward

On **continuous** traffic (one sample per minute), subquery steps equal real minutes and the duty ratio is exact. That is the assumed customer condition.

On a **gapped** series, carry-forward inflates the numerator when a gap **follows** a breaching sample. Worked example: breach at minute 0, gap through minute 4, healthy 5–9 → BREACH_STEPS 5 / TOTAL_STEPS 10 = 0.50 from one real breaching minute.

The one real-world case is a breach immediately followed by the source region going silent — a genuine failover signature — where the board briefly over-scores before liveness flips it to **NO DATA - FEED SILENT**. That is accepted behaviour, not a defect.

The durable fix is a Prometheus recording rule materialising the breach boolean at scrape time (production answer; not built here).

A namespace that breaches every *third* minute yields 4-in-10 and escapes a 5-in-10 (50%) duty gate. That is a deliberate trade, not an oversight. Missing minutes count as **not-breaching**.

### Single-namespace severity limit

The severity path requires at least `$breadth_min` breaching namespaces (default 2) and is therefore **inert on a single-namespace view** — the framed customer case when the board is scoped to one namespace. There the **sustained path is the only route to FAILOVER?**.

### Liveness (correction to the reference design)

Liveness is measured on the namespace's **full** `temporal_cloud_v1_service_request_count` stream in the selected region — **not** on the gated experience APIs and not on a latency series. A quiet experience API is not a silent region (measured: 0 experience-API latency series vs 7 request-count series emitting in the same 7-minute window). This is a **correction to the reference board's design**, not just a port of it.

Resulting states that must stay distinct:

- Feed flowing, not enough to judge → **TOO FEW REQUESTS** (grey)
- Nothing emitting in namespace+region → **NO DATA - FEED SILENT** (purple)
- Judged healthy → **CLEAR** (dark)

### Namespace scope and liveness masking

Default the namespace control to a **single** namespace with traffic. A failover decision is about one namespace at a time. Multi-select remains available so the severity breadth path can see multiple namespaces when you deliberately widen scope.

When more than one namespace is selected, liveness `sum()`s `service_request_count` across the selection: a busy namespace can mask a silent one, so a namespace that has actually failed over may render **TOO FEW REQUESTS** instead of **NO DATA - FEED SILENT**. Judge one namespace at a time for a failover decision.

With a single namespace selected, `$breadth_min = 2` makes the severity path inert, so the **sustained path is the only route to FAILOVER?** — same limit as in the single-namespace severity note above; the two statements are one rule.

### Absent by design

Success ratio, platform overload, and throttle cause-attribution are **out of scope**: `resource_exhausted_cause` does not exist on the customer OpenMetrics surface, and `service_error_count` has no error-class dimension. Nexus is excluded deliberately (wrong input to "fail over *this* namespace").

### This board cannot confirm recovery in the target region

The Decision row is source-region-scoped. Replication lag in Context is replica-region-labelled and is **context, not a gate** (Temporal-owned, no SLA).

### Production hardening (not in this board)

Prefer Prometheus recording rules that pre-materialize the volume-banded gating / breach boolean at one-minute resolution so windowed counts can use raw ranges on selectors. That is the durable fix for the sparse-series / subquery carry-forward class.

## Sync Request Health

These are the three **experience APIs** the failover gate watches: `StartWorkflowExecution`, `SignalWorkflowExecution`, and `SignalWithStartWorkflowExecution`.

Latency is in **seconds**. Percentiles (`p50` / `p95` / `p99`) are **pre-computed by Temporal Cloud** — do not average or otherwise aggregate them across operations (that would not produce a real percentile).

Operations with no traffic render **empty by design** — an empty Signal panel means this workload has not exercised that API, not that the query is broken. Panels are scoped to the selected **source** `$region` (default `aws-us-east-1`); do not roll up both HA regions here.

panels.title: StartWorkflowExecution latency
panels.description: Pre-computed Cloud OpenMetrics percentiles for StartWorkflowExecution (seconds). Not aggregated across operations. Empty when this operation has no traffic - by design. Threshold line is a twin of $lat_ceiling_s (default 0.2); changing the variable does not move this line - update the yellow step by hand.

panels.title: SignalWorkflowExecution latency
panels.description: Pre-computed Cloud OpenMetrics percentiles for SignalWorkflowExecution (seconds). Not aggregated across operations. Empty when this operation has no traffic - by design. Threshold line is a twin of $lat_ceiling_s (default 0.2); changing the variable does not move this line - update the yellow step by hand.

panels.title: SignalWithStartWorkflowExecution latency
panels.description: Pre-computed Cloud OpenMetrics percentiles for SignalWithStartWorkflowExecution (seconds). Not aggregated across operations. Empty when this operation has no traffic - by design. Threshold line is a twin of $lat_ceiling_s (default 0.2); changing the variable does not move this line - update the yellow step by hand.

panels.title: Experience API volume (requests / 5 min)
panels.description: Unit: requests per 5 minutes. Converts the Cloud per-second rate: avg_over_time(temporal_cloud_v1_service_request_count[5m]) * 300. Companion to the volume bands on the Decision gate ($min_requests / $p99_min_requests). Scoped to selected source $region.

options.content:
## Context

Replication lag into the HA **replica** region. This is context for a failover decision, **not a gate**. Scoped by namespace only - the `region` label on these series is the replica/target, not the source.

panels.title: Replication lag (replica region)
panels.description: temporal_cloud_v1_replication_lag_p50/p95/p99 in seconds. Replication lag is Temporal-owned and carries no SLA; it is context for a failover decision, not a gate; and it only exists for namespaces with a multi-region HA replica. Scoped by ${namespace} ONLY - the region label is the REPLICA (target), not the source. Filtering by the Decision-row source ${region} would render this panel empty against a healthy metric (false 'no data'). Empty state: no replica configured / no data - never treat as healthy.

list.name: datasource
list.description: Prometheus datasource. Default uid prometheus-kind (host metrics store). All panels use ${datasource}.

list.name: namespace
list.label: Namespace
list.description: Temporal Cloud namespace label (temporal_namespace). No saved default - Grafana selects the first value from the label query (a single real namespace on any account). Multi-select remains available so severity breadth can be widened deliberately; with multiple namespaces selected, liveness is an aggregate and can mask a silent namespace (see Method panel). Used by Sync Request Health, Failover gate, Latency breach table, and Context replication lag.

list.name: region
list.label: Region
list.description: Unit: Temporal Cloud region label. Default aws-us-east-1 = active SOURCE region. HA replica also emits service_request_count under aws-us-west-2, so this dropdown lists both — keep Decision and Sync Request Health scoped to the single selected source region; do not aggregate across regions. Context replication lag is scoped by namespace only (its region label is the REPLICA/target). Twins: Sync Request Health latency/volume panels; Failover gate verdict; Latency breach table.

list.name: exp_ops
list.description: Regex for operation=~"$exp_ops". The three experience APIs the gate watches. Used by Sync Request Health volume panel, Failover gate verdict, and Latency breach table. Unitless regex — not a display value.

list.name: lat_ceiling_s
list.label: Latency ceiling (s)
list.description: Unit: seconds. Inherited customer calibration (1,190-account scan); unvalidated on this surface. Default 0.2s ≈ published p99 SLO. Changing this rescores the gate/table but does NOT move drawn threshold lines — update the threshold step on StartWorkflowExecution latency, SignalWorkflowExecution latency, and SignalWithStartWorkflowExecution latency to match. Also twins: Failover gate verdict (breach compare), Latency breach table (multiple-of-ceiling).

list.name: sustain_min
list.label: Sustained breach (min)
list.description: Unit: minutes (honest samples) / also the numerator of the duty threshold ($sustain_min / $sustain_window_min). Sustained path fires when duty >= that ratio AND honest samples in the window >= $sustain_min. Inherited calibration. Twins: Failover gate verdict; Latency breach table colour steps on est. breach minutes (hardcoded - update by hand); any prose naming the 5-in-10 duty cycle.

list.name: sustain_window_min
list.label: Sustain window (min)
list.description: Unit: minutes. Denominator of the duty threshold ($sustain_min / $sustain_window_min) and the window length for BREACH_STEPS / TOTAL_STEPS / HONEST_SAMPLES. Default 10 with sustain_min 5 => 50% duty. Twins: Failover gate verdict; Latency breach table windowed columns; Method prose naming the duty cycle.

list.name: eval_window_min
list.label: Eval window (min)
list.description: Unit: minutes. Lookback for the Latency breach table's Peak gating (s) and Multiple of ceiling columns (max_over_time over this window). Does NOT scope the Failover gate verdict - that uses sustain_window_min / stale_grace_min / publication_lag_min. Twin: breach table peak columns.

list.name: stale_grace_min
list.label: Stale grace (min)
list.description: Unit: minutes. Liveness lookback. Default 7 (measured publication lag ~209s / ~3.5 min; a 3-minute window is permanently empty here). Liveness is count_over_time(temporal_cloud_v1_service_request_count{temporal_namespace, region}[${stale_grace_min}m]) on the namespace's FULL request stream in the selected region — no operation filter. A quiet experience API is not a silent region (Correction 04: measured 0 p99 experience-API series vs 7 request_count series in the same 7-minute window). Splits TOO FEW REQUESTS (feed flowing) from NO DATA - FEED SILENT (nothing emitting). Twins: Failover gate verdict liveness fallthrough.

list.name: publication_lag_min
list.label: Publication lag (min)
list.description: Unit: minutes. Offset for windowed breach/duty counts, honest-sample raw ranges, AND the lagged instant terms (WATCH_BOOL, SEVERITY_BOOL, gating-presence). Measured endpoint publication lag ~209s (~3.5 min). Default 4 clears that lag. Offset alone does not fix subquery carry-forward across mid-window gaps on gapped series — the sustained path uses duty cycle for that. Do NOT apply this offset to the liveness check (stale_grace_min). Twins: Failover gate sustained + lagged instant terms; Latency breach table duty/honest/est columns.

list.name: sev_multiple
list.label: Severity multiple
list.description: Unit: multiple of lat_ceiling_s (unitless). Inherited calibration from the 1,190-account scan (default 25). Severity path fires when BOTH hold: (1) breadth — at least $breadth_min namespaces currently breaching the latency ceiling; (2) magnitude — the peak gating latency across ALL gating series in the selected region is >= sev_multiple * lat_ceiling_s. Breadth and magnitude are deliberately NOT coupled per-namespace (matches the reference design's region-wide-event signature). Consequence: one namespace at 25x plus one at 1.05x satisfies the path. Twin: Failover gate verdict only.

list.name: breadth_min
list.label: Severity breadth (namespaces)
list.description: Unit: distinct namespaces. Minimum namespaces breaching in the SAME minute for the severity path. Failover is regional — one-namespace breach is a workload problem. Twin: Failover gate verdict only.

list.name: p99_min_requests
list.label: p99 volume floor (req/5m)
list.description: Unit: requests per 5 minutes (avg_over_time(request_count[5m])*300). At or above this volume, p99 gates. Between this and min_requests, p95 gates. Inherited; unvalidated here. Twins: Failover gate verdict volume band; Latency breach table volume-band column; Sync Request Health volume panel is the human-readable companion.

list.name: min_requests
list.label: Min volume to judge (req/5m)
list.description: Unit: requests per 5 minutes. Below this → no gating series (not judged: grey / collapses to NO DATA when also outside stale_grace). Absence must not render as CLEAR. Inherited; unvalidated here. Twins: Failover gate verdict volume band; Latency breach table Volume band column; Sync Request Health volume panel.
